source_refs.note: Topic 4.1.1.4 Applications of Lists (PDF 95, printed 92). Short question 7 is answered; the adjacency-list remark is general knowledge, flagged.

items: Data storage and manipulation: records, entries and values, with easy insertion, deletion and access.
Stack and queue implementations: lists can implement stacks (LIFO) and queues (FIFO).
Sorting and searching: bubble sort, selection sort and binary search often work on lists.
Function arguments: lists pass multiple values to a function.
Matrix operations: a list of lists can represent the rows of a matrix.

blocks.prompt: How can lists be used to implement other data structures (short question 7)?
blocks.explanation: A stack uses append() to push and pop() to remove from the end; a queue uses append() to enqueue and pop(0) to dequeue from the front; a tree node keeps a list of its children; and a graph can keep, for each vertex, a list of its neighbours (an adjacency list). A list of lists also makes a matrix.

items: Lists store data, build stacks and queues, feed sorting and searching, pass arguments and form matrices.
